articles.title: Recruiters search booleans, not keywords
articles.excerpt: Recruiters do not read your resume the way a human reads a novel. They run queries through an applicant tracking system using boolean operators like Python AND (Django OR FastAPI) NOT junior. If your…
articles.body: Recruiters do not read your resume the way a human reads a novel. They run queries through an applicant tracking system using boolean operators like Python AND (Django OR FastAPI) NOT junior. If your application lists technologies as a random inventory list at the bottom of the page, the query misses the connective tissue. Context is what makes a boolean match stick. A single keyword passes an initial keyword scan, but a project sentence passes the logic of the search. If the recruiter looks for FastAPI production experience, listing FastAPI in a skills block is weak. Writing that you migrated a payment service from Flask to FastAPI under load gives the query terms proximity. Proximity rules the search results.

articles.body: Author: Nweibong Emmanuel Praise Category: Cloud Computing Case Study: Amazon Web Services – Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) Abstract The increasing demand for digital services has made traditional computing infrastructure increasingly challenging for some organizations to maintain. Businesses, universities and other institutions require computing resources that can support their applications, store information and accommodate changes in user demand. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) provides an alternative by allowing organizations to access computing resources through cloud service providers without having to purchase and maintain all the physical equipment themselves.

articles.title: Hugging Face AnySpeechRecognizer: swap Apple, Parakeet or Qwen3-ASR without rewriting your STT path
articles.excerpt: On 29 October 2026 Hugging Face (via Mattt) released two open Swift packages aimed at Apple platforms: AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel. The first gives you a SpeechAnalyzer-shaped API so you…
articles.body: On 29 October 2026 Hugging Face (via Mattt) released two open Swift packages aimed at Apple platforms: AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel. The first gives you a SpeechAnalyzer-shaped API so you can keep the same capture and session code while swapping the underlying recognizer. The second returns typed yes/no, choice or score results with probabilities instead of forcing you to parse free-form generation. What AnySpeechRecognizer actually ships It implements the shape of Apple’s newer SpeechAnalyzer API. Default backend is Apple’s own Speech framework. You can also point it at Core ML conversions of NVIDIA Parakeet (derived from Parakeet + Moondream work) or Alibaba’s Qwen3-ASR 0.6B / 1.7B. Parakeet v3 covers roughly 25 European languages.

articles.title: Designing an idle RPG economy in vanilla JS: lessons from Snow317.io
articles.excerpt: Snow317.io is a small 8-bit clicker RPG we're building in plain JavaScript: no framework, no engine, one page. You click ATTACK, monsters drop coins, and coins buy weapons, armour and pets. Pets deal…
articles.body: Snow317.io is a small 8-bit clicker RPG we're building in plain JavaScript: no framework, no engine, one page. You click ATTACK, monsters drop coins, and coins buy weapons, armour and pets. Pets deal damage for you. It's a spin-off of SnowRSPS, a custom game server we've run since 2012. The code is easy. The economy is the hard part. Here's what we've learned so far. 1. Pick your growth curves before you write content Every incremental game comes down to two curves: Income growth : how fast coins per second rise Cost growth : how fast prices rise If costs grow faster than income, the player hits a wall. If income grows faster, the game is "solved" in an afternoon. The usual pattern is exponential costs and multiplicative income: const cost = ( base , owned , rate = 1.15 ) => Math .

articles.title: Logging AI tool usage without logging sensitive data
articles.excerpt: When a team adds an AI feature, the first debugging instinct is to log everything: the full prompt, the full response, the user's message. It works. It also means your logs now hold a copy of every cu…
articles.body: When a team adds an AI feature, the first debugging instinct is to log everything: the full prompt, the full response, the user's message. It works. It also means your logs now hold a copy of every customer email, contract and support ticket that went through the feature, sitting in a system with weaker access controls than your database and a much longer memory. You need logs. You need them to debug bad answers, answer audit questions and keep costs under control. You don't need them to be a second copy of your customers' data. Here's a practical middle path. Decide what the logs are for Before writing any code, list the questions your logs must answer. For most small teams it's these: Debugging: which prompt version and model produced this answer, and did the call fail?

Reddit’s about to look and feel a lot different, and no, I’m not just talking about the new For You and Following feeds the platform announced yesterday. Reddit is planning something much bigger — something that could fundamentally change how millions access the platform.

articles.title: Bethesda Pays Tribute to Patrick Stewart for His Role in Oblivion, Fans Remember His Role in Games Like Castlevania
articles.excerpt: Bethesda has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart for his role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion after his death.
articles.body: Bethesda has paid tribute to Sir Patrick Stewart for his role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion after his death. Earlier today, it was announced that beloved actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, died at 86 years old . The news came as a shock to many, and social media has been full of tributes to the actor. Many of his longtime collaborators, such as William Shatner, Kevin Feige, and Hugh Jackman all shared kind words about their time working with him. Bethesda also offered up its own tribute by acknowledging the actor's death, calling him an "inspiration to us all." Stewart had a brief role in The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion as Emperor Uriel Septim VII, who is killed off at the very beginning of the game.

articles.title: Halloween Aboard the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit.…
articles.body: ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano finally gets his wish to fly like Superman aboard the International Space Station during Expedition 37. Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit. Whether individually or as an entire crew, they dress up in sometimes spooky, sometimes scary, but always creative costumes, often designed from materials available aboard the space station.   Take a look at how the station crews have celebrated in years past. For Halloween 2009, the Expedition 21 crew shows off its costumes. Expedition 21 NASA astronaut Nicole Stott shows off her Halloween costume.

articles.title: James Gunn Says It 'Won't Be Too Long' Before DCU Batman Is Cast, Will Be Close in Age to David Corenswet's Superman
articles.excerpt: James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman.
articles.body: James Gunn has revealed that DC Studios is finally getting ready to cast the DCU's Batman. Speaking on a new podcast about James Gunn's Suicide Squad film, the director and DC Studios boss addressed where he's at when it comes to the next Batman. Although Robert Pattinson is playing the current caped crusader, it's expected that he will exist in his own separate universe , away from James Gunn's DCU, while another Batman will join forces with the likes of Superman. He noted that it "won't be too long" before they begin casting the next Batman and debunked rumors that he's already been cast. He noted that he's open to casting anyone for the role, even if they've been in a previous DC movie like The Suicide Squad.
